title: Sentence Transformers and open models on Hugging Face

videos.script: Every vector in the last two lessons came from somebody else's server. This lesson brings the model home. {{home}} An open model is a file you download once. After that it runs on your own machine. There is no bill, no rate limit, and no customer message leaves the building. {{file}} Most open embedding models live on Hugging Face, and most people run them with one library, sentence-transformers. {{library}} This lab cannot reach Hugging Face. So you will see that code, and then run the same model another way, through a fifty-line file you can read to the end. {{fifty}} Inside, there are four steps. Cut the text into pieces. Run the transformer. Average the pieces. Scale the result to length one. {{steps}} Then you will find the limit nobody warns you about. This model reads two hundred and fifty-six pieces, and quietly drops the rest. {{limit}} You will learn to read a model card, where that limit is written down. {{card}} You will measure two models on the help centre's own questions, and ask what that measurement does and does not prove. {{measure}} And you will time them on a processor, because on your own machine speed is your problem too. {{speed}}
